did_you_know.text: Did you know? Manasseh became king at the age of twelve and reigned in Jerusalem for fifty-five years.
Did you know? Manasseh rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had demolished, erected altars to the Baals and Asherahs, and worshiped and served the army of heaven.
Did you know? Manasseh even built altars in the house of the LORD, although it was the place where the LORD's name was to be honored in Jerusalem.

Did you know? Scripture lists among Manasseh's deeds the sacrifice of his sons in the fire, practicing sorcery and divination, and consulting mediums and spiritists; in this way he did much evil in the eyes of the LORD.
Did you know? The LORD spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they did not listen to his warnings.
Did you know? The commanders of the king of Assyria captured Manasseh, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon.
Did you know? It was precisely in his distress that Manasseh humbled himself greatly before the God of his ancestors and prayed to him.
Did you know? According to Scripture, the LORD answered Manasseh's prayer, brought him back to Jerusalem and his kingdom, and then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God.
Did you know? After his return, Manasseh removed the idols, the carved image, and the altars he had built, and threw them out of the city.
Did you know? Even after Manasseh's reforms, the people still sacrificed at the high places; however, according to Scripture, they sacrificed to the LORD their God.
